flags.title: Unstable or stable angina?
flags.concern: The pain is predictable, exertional and relieved by rest over three months, which fits stable angina, yet it is labelled unstable angina. If it is truly unstable, outpatient cardiology next week and a stress test would be too slow.
flags.consider: Consider clarifying rest pain or a crescendo pattern, and either sending her for same-day evaluation with troponins if unstable, or relabelling as stable angina for outpatient testing.

evidence.quote: it mainly happens when i'm walking
my suspicion is you have something called unstable angina
we will try to get you into cardiology the next week and get you set up for some sort of a stress test

flags.title: Consistent nitroglycerin and 911 instructions?
flags.concern: She was first told to go to hospital if pain persists after one or two pills, then told she may take up to three pills five minutes apart, which could delay emergency care for a possible heart attack.
flags.consider: Consider giving one clear instruction, for example calling 911 if pain is not improved five minutes after the first dose, and putting it in writing.

evidence.quote: if it does n't go away after one or two pills i want you to go to the hospital
so you can take it up to three pills every five minutes

flags.title: Statin and lipid panel for suspected CAD?
flags.concern: A 53-year-old with diabetes and suspected coronary disease was started on aspirin only; lipids, statin therapy and an anti-anginal agent were not discussed.
flags.consider: Consider checking a lipid panel and starting statin therapy, and possibly an anti-anginal such as a beta-blocker while awaiting cardiology.

evidence.quote: i'm gon na go ahead and start you on some aspirin daily

flags.title: HCTZ as first choice with diabetes?
flags.concern: Hypertension is not yet confirmed, and a thiazide can raise glucose and alter electrolytes in a diabetic patient; no baseline kidney function or electrolytes were ordered and sulfa allergy was not asked.
flags.consider: Consider confirming BP with home readings, checking a basic metabolic panel and urine albumin, asking about sulfa allergy, and weighing an ACE inhibitor or ARB given her diabetes.

evidence.quote: we have n't really diagnosed you with that yet
i'm gon na go ahead and start you on some hydrochlorothiazide
sometimes you can have a cross reaction with some other medications like sulfa medications
